transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

No matter how interested I am, I just can’t keep my attention on job training or applications long enough to finish them. It’s incredibly frustrating because I really want to start my career, but I just get stuck and can't seem to follow through on any of it.
Did you have similar problems with attention, finishing schoolwork, or being easily distracted when you were a child, before age 12? Or did these concentration problems start only more recently?

Yeah, it definitely goes way back to when I was a kid. In elementary school, my teachers were constantly moving my seat and sending notes home because I'd blurt out answers, wander around the classroom, and always lose my homework. I wasn't trying to cause trouble, but I just couldn't keep it together even back then.

Do these attention and restlessness problems still happen in more than one part of your life now, like at home, with friends, or during daily tasks—not just with job training or applications? How much do they interfere with your day-to-day functioning?

Yes, they affect almost every part of my life, not just work. At home, I'm always pacing, interrupting conversations, and forgetting basic things like paying my bills or showing up for appointments. It severely interferes with my life—I've lost several garage jobs, missed a major training program intake because I forgot the date, and now I'm stuck living with my parents and falling behind financially.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent pattern since childhood of both inattention (difficulty sustaining attention, losing homework, forgetting bills/appointments, failing to follow through) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (blurting out answers, wandering around class, pacing, interrupting conversations) across multiple settings, with clear functional impairment in work, training, and daily life. Onset before age 12 and cross-situational impairment are explicitly confirmed, supporting ADHD, predominantly inattentive type code as provided in the candidate set.
